newsitem.title: USA: CBOT wheat ends lower on IGC estimate, positioning.
newsitem.headline: CBOT wheat ends lower on IGC estimate, positioning.

text.p: End-of-the-month position squaring, including long liquidation, plus an estimate for world wheat production by the International Grains Council pressed CBOT wheat futures to a lower close, traders said.
"The IGC estimate wasn't a shock but there's nothing bullish in it," a trader said.
The IGC Friday pegged 1996 world wheat output at 563 million tonnes, up from its previous forecast for 560 million tonnes.
Slow exports of U.S. wheat and good harvest weather for U.S. spring wheat also pressed the market.

But declines were curbed by lighter-than-expected deliveries posted Friday against the September contracts. CBOT said 500,000 bushels were posted for delivery, well below estimates for 2.0 million to 5.0 million bushels. Nearby September gained quietly on spreads with the December.
Trading was quiet and volume was thin before the three-day holiday weekend. CBOT grain and soy complex futures will not trade Monday as the exchange observes the U.S. Labor Day holiday.
Wheat closed 1-1/2 to five cents per bushel lower, with September down 2-3/4 at $4.48-1/2 a bushel.
Wheat futures volume was estimated at 14,500 contracts, down from 18,680 Thursday.
In wheat options, Cargill Investor Services sold 200 December $4.70 calls at 13 cents and Refco Inc sold 150 December $4.90 calls at 7-1/4 to nine cents, traders said.
Wheat options volume was estimated at 2,000 contracts, down from 3,754 Thursday.
